introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the phenomenon of emission of electrons from a sufficiently heated metal surface.
questions.corrige_markdown: This phenomenon is **thermionic emission**: when a metal is heated to a high temperature, some of its conduction electrons gain enough thermal (kinetic) energy to overcome the surface potential barrier (the work function of the metal) and escape from the surface.

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the speed with which the electrons leave the anode.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The electrons start from rest at the filament and are accelerated through a potential difference $V = 2000\ \mathrm{V}$. The work done on each electron by the field becomes kinetic energy:

$$eV = \tfrac12 m v^{2}$$
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{2eV}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{2\times1.60\times10^{-19}\times2000}{9.11\times10^{-31}}} = \sqrt{7.03\times10^{14}}$$

**$v = 2.65\times10^{7}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.** (This is about $0.09\,c$, so the non-relativistic formula is adequate.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Upon leaving the anode, the electrons enter into a region of cross magnetic and electric fields as shown in *figure 3*. If the intensity of the electric field is $7.5\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, calculate the flux density of the magnetic field if the electrons pass through the cross fields undeflected as shown in figure 3.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The electrons are undeflected when the electric force and the magnetic force on each electron are **equal in magnitude and opposite in direction**:

- The field $E$ points downward, so the electric force on a (negative) electron points **upward**, $F_E = eE$.
- For $\mathbf{v}$ to the right and $\mathbf{B}$ into the page, the magnetic force on the electron (Fleming's left-hand rule, with conventional current to the left) points **downward**, $F_B = Bev$. The two forces therefore oppose each other, as needed.

$$eE = Bev \;\Rightarrow\; B = \frac{E}{v} = \frac{7.5\times10^{4}}{2.65\times10^{7}} = 2.83\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T}$$

**$B \approx 2.8\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T}$ (2.8 mT).** The result does not depend on the charge of the particle, only on its speed.
